description: Capture the frontmost app's UI as a numbered list of elements: e12 is label 12 for Click, Type, Scroll and Move. Params: use_vision (add a screenshot), use_annotation (draw the labels on it), app (another app). Call it first and after the UI changes.

app.description: App name or bundle id (default: the frontmost app).

use_annotation.description: With use_vision: draw the labels on the image.

use_dom.description: Ignored: web content is in the accessibility tree.

use_ui_tree.description: Ignored: the element list is always returned.

use_vision.description: Include a screenshot of the window.

name: Snapshot
title: Snapshot an app's UI

description: Capture a display (display=[index]) or a region ([left, top, right, bottom] in screen points) as an image. Coordinates on macOS are points; the result gives the scale.

use_annotation.description: Ignored (use Snapshot with use_vision for labels).

name: Screenshot
title: Take a screenshot

description:
Find elements by text, role or identifier in an app window; with scroll=true, scroll its list or page
until a match appears (lazily loaded lists, long settings panes, feeds).
Use it instead of scrolling and snapshotting by hand. Params: text (fuzzy: exact > prefix > substring >
words), role (button, row, field… or an AX role), identifier (AXIdentifier); app / window_id; container
(ref of the list/page to search and scroll; default: the whole window, scrolling its largest scroll
area); scroll; max_scrolls (≤ 50); limit.
Returns matches (ref, role, name, score) from the final snapshot, found, scrolls, at_end and
searched_all. Not finding anything is not an error: found=false with what was searched.
Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT, APP_NOT_FOUND, STALE_REF (container), BLOCKED_BY_POLICY, USER_ACTIVE.

app.description: Target app: name ('Notes'), bundle id ('com.apple.Notes') or pid. Default: the frontmost app.

container.description: Ref of a scroll area, list, table, web area or text area (or of an element inside one), e.g. "e13".

scroll.description: Scroll the container until a match appears.

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the ref belongs to. Default: the latest snapshot.

timeout_ms.description: Time budget in milliseconds; partial results come back when it runs out.

window_id.description: Window id from list_windows; scopes the call to that window.

name: Find
title: Find elements

description:
Map an app in one call: its windows, menu bar (top-level menus with item counts), toolbar buttons,
tabs, sidebar sections, scroll areas, open dialogs and the focused element, plus how well AXPilot can
drive it (app kind, accessibility quality, strategies, tips).
Call it first for an unfamiliar app, then snapshot for the full element list. Params: app / window_id.
Returns a compact overview with refs (usable with click, read, scroll…) and the snapshot_id they belong
to. Errors: APP_NOT_FOUND, WINDOW_NOT_FOUND, PERMISSION_ACCESSIBILITY, BLOCKED_BY_POLICY, TIMEOUT.

app.description: Target app: name ('Notes'), bundle id ('com.apple.Notes') or pid. Default: the frontmost app.

window_id.description: Window id from list_windows; scopes the call to that window.

name: Explore
title: Explore an app

description:
Read the whole content of a long list, table, document, text view or web page: AXPilot scrolls through
it page by page and joins the pages without repeats.
Use it for long chats, documents, logs, mailboxes and search results instead of scrolling by hand.
Params: target ("auto": the window's main scrollable area, or the ref of a list/table/web area/text
area); app / window_id (with "auto"); mode (auto | rows | text); from_top (start at the top, default
true); max_pages (≤ 30); restore (scroll back to where it was); timeout_ms.
Returns the lines (rows: cells joined by " | "), pages, scrolls, complete (everything from the top to
the end) and at_end. Partial content comes back with complete=false and a warning when a limit is
reached. Errors: STALE_REF, APP_NOT_FOUND, BLOCKED_BY_POLICY, USER_ACTIVE, PAUSED_BY_USER.

app.description: Target app: name ('Notes'), bundle id ('com.apple.Notes') or pid. Default: the frontmost app.

from_top.description: Scroll to the top first, so the whole content is read.

restore.description: Scroll back to the original position afterwards.

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the ref belongs to. Default: the latest snapshot.

target.description: "auto" (the main scrollable area) or the ref of a list, table, web area or text area.

timeout_ms.description: Time budget in milliseconds; partial results come back when it runs out.

window_id.description: Window id from list_windows; scopes the call to that window.

name: Read
title: Read long content

description:
Show everything about one element: all accessibility attributes, supported actions, its
ancestors (path from the window) and children.
Use it when a snapshot line is not enough: to learn which actions an element supports, why it
is disabled, its identifier or exact value. Params: ref (from a snapshot), snapshot_id (default:
the latest snapshot). Errors: STALE_REF (the element is gone: take a new snapshot),
SNAPSHOT_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_ARGUMENT (malformed ref), BLOCKED_BY_POLICY.

ref.description: Element ref from a snapshot, e.g. "e12" (or "s_ab12:e12" to pin the snapshot).

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the ref belongs to. Default: the latest snapshot.

name: Inspect
title: Inspect an element

description:
Read the text on screen with OCR, with the position of each line.
Use it for text the accessibility tree does not expose (images, canvases, remote desktops,
games, some custom-drawn apps). For text in normal apps, snapshot(mode="text") is faster and exact.
Params: window_id | app | rect | display_id (at most one; default: the frontmost window),
languages (e.g. ["en-US"]). Returns lines top-to-bottom with their center points and a
screenshot_id for pixel mapping. To click a line, use snapshot(mode="vision") and its o-ref, or
the center point. Errors: PERMISSION_SCREEN_RECORDING, WINDOW_NOT_FOUND, APP_NOT_FOUND,
DISPLAY_NOT_FOUND, BLOCKED_BY_POLICY, TIMEOUT.

app.description: Capture the front window of this app (name, bundle id or pid).

display_id.description: Display id from list_displays. Default: the main display.

rect.description: Region [x, y, width, height] in screen points (e.g. a frame from a snapshot).

window_id.description: Window id from list_windows; scopes the call to that window.

name: OCR
title: Read text with OCR

description:
List running apps (name, bundle id, pid, frontmost/hidden), optionally with installed apps that
are not running. Use it to find the exact name or bundle id to pass as `App`, or to check
whether an app is running. Apps blocked by the safety policy are marked. Params: include_installed.

include_installed.description: Also list installed apps that are not running.

name: ListApps
title: List apps

description:
List on-screen windows front-to-back: window_id, app, title, frame, focused/minimized state.
Use it to pick a window_id for snapshot, screenshot or the window tool, or to see which windows
an app has open. Params: app (default: all apps). Titles of windows blocked by the safety policy
are withheld. Errors: APP_NOT_FOUND.

app.description: Target app: name ('Notes'), bundle id ('com.apple.Notes') or pid. Default: the frontmost app.

name: ListWindows
title: List windows

description:
List displays with their id, frame and work area (in points, origin top-left of the main
display) and scale factor. Use it before capturing or moving windows on multi-monitor setups.
name: DisplayInventory
title: List displays

description: Pause for duration seconds (at most 60).
name: Wait
title: Wait for a condition

description: Wait (polling) until text_exists, active_window, element_exists, element_enabled or focused_element holds for text / window_name in the frontmost app, up to timeout seconds (at most 60).

interval.description: Ignored: AXPilot chooses the polling interval.

text.description: Text, element name or window title.

use_dom.description: Ignored: web content is in the accessibility tree.

name: WaitFor
title: Wait for a condition

description:
Report AXPilot's state: version, engine, macOS version, permissions (Accessibility, Screen
Recording), whether the user paused it (kill switch), the input lock, the active profile and
enabled tools, rate limit and confirmation mode.
Use it first when tools fail with permission errors, or to check what this server can do.
name: ControlStatus
title: AXPilot status

description: Click an element (label) or a point (loc). label is the number of a snapshot ref (12 for e12); loc is [x, y] in macOS screen points. button left|right|middle; clicks 1-3. Returns what changed.

label.description: Element label: the number of a snapshot ref (12 for e12).

loc.description: [x, y] in macOS screen points (from a snapshot).

name: Click
title: Click

description: Select several items (files, rows, checkboxes): clicks each of locs ([[x, y], …]) or labels ([12, 13, …]) while holding cmd (press_ctrl=true), or plain clicks (press_ctrl=false).

press_ctrl.description: Hold cmd to add each item to the selection.

name: MultiSelect
title: Click

description: Type text into a field (label or loc; default: the focused field). label is the number of a snapshot ref (12 for e12); loc is [x, y] in macOS screen points. clear replaces the text; caret_position start|end moves the caret first; press_enter presses Return.

caret_position.description: Move the caret to the start or end first (idle: leave it).

label.description: Element label: the number of a snapshot ref (12 for e12).

loc.description: [x, y] in macOS screen points (from a snapshot).

name: Type
title: Type text

description: Press keys: "cmd+c", "cmd+shift+t", "return", or several separated by spaces ("cmd+a delete"). macOS shortcuts use cmd where Windows uses ctrl; win means cmd.

shortcut.description: Keys joined by +, e.g. "cmd+c" (cmd, not ctrl); several: separate by spaces.

name: Shortcut
title: Press keys

description: Scroll at a label, a loc or the pointer. label is the number of a snapshot ref (12 for e12); loc is [x, y] in macOS screen points. direction up|down|left|right (type horizontal turns up/down into left/right); wheel_times notches of 3 lines.

label.description: Element label: the number of a snapshot ref (12 for e12).

loc.description: [x, y] in macOS screen points (from a snapshot).

name: Scroll
title: Scroll

description: Move the pointer to a label or loc (hover), or drag=true to drag to it from from_loc (default: the pointer) over duration seconds. label is the number of a snapshot ref (12 for e12); loc is [x, y] in macOS screen points.

from_loc.description: drag: [x, y] to start from (default: the pointer).

label.description: Element label: the number of a snapshot ref (12 for e12).

loc.description: [x, y] in macOS screen points (from a snapshot).

name: Move
title: Move the mouse

description:
Set a control to a value, the way its role expects:
- checkbox / switch / toggle / radio: "true" or "false" (on/off). Idempotent: nothing happens if
  it is already in that state.
- slider / stepper: a number (clamped to the control's range; a warning says so).
- disclosure triangle: "true" (expanded) or "false" (collapsed).
- text field / search field / text area / combo box: the new text (replaces it).
- date picker: an ISO 8601 date, "2026-10-20" or "2026-10-20 14:30"; a time field: "14:30".
- pop-up button: the title of the option to choose.
Params: ref, value (always a string), snapshot_id, report. The result says whether anything
changed. Errors: ELEMENT_NOT_ACTIONABLE (read-only or disabled), INVALID_ARGUMENT (e.g. not a
number for a slider), BLOCKED_BY_POLICY (secure fields), STALE_REF.

ref.description: Element ref from a snapshot, e.g. "e12" (or "s_ab12:e12" to pin the snapshot).

report.description: What to return after acting: "diff" (what changed, default), "snapshot" (the whole new snapshot) or "none" (fastest).

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the ref belongs to. Default: the latest snapshot.

value.description: The value as text: "true"/"false", a number, or text.

name: SetValue
title: Set a control's value

description:
Choose an option of a control by its title (or 1-based index): a pop-up button or combo box
(AXPilot opens it and picks the item), a radio group, tab group or segmented control (presses the
matching button), or a list, table or outline (selects the matching row).
Params: ref (the control, from a snapshot), option (title: exact, then prefix, then substring; pop-ups
and combo boxes need the exact title, since their items are listed only while open) or index (not
for pop-ups); snapshot_id; report. Choosing the option that is already selected changes nothing.
Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT (no or several matching options: the message lists them), STALE_REF,
ELEMENT_NOT_ACTIONABLE (disabled, or not a control with options; menu buttons: use
perform_action AXShowMenu), BLOCKED_BY_POLICY, USER_ACTIVE, PAUSED_BY_USER.

ref.description: The control: a pop-up, combo box, radio/tab group or list ("e7").

report.description: What to return after acting: "diff" (what changed, default), "snapshot" (the whole new snapshot) or "none" (fastest).

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the ref belongs to. Default: the latest snapshot.

name: SelectOption
title: Choose an option

description:
Perform an accessibility action on an element: AXPress, AXShowMenu (context menu), AXIncrement,
AXDecrement, AXConfirm, AXCancel, AXRaise (bring a window forward), AXPick, AXOpen…
The element's supported actions are listed in its snapshot entry and in inspect.
Params: ref, action, snapshot_id, report. Errors: ELEMENT_NOT_ACTIONABLE (unsupported action or
disabled element), STALE_REF, BLOCKED_BY_POLICY, INVALID_ARGUMENT.

ref.description: Element ref from a snapshot, e.g. "e12" (or "s_ab12:e12" to pin the snapshot).

report.description: What to return after acting: "diff" (what changed, default), "snapshot" (the whole new snapshot) or "none" (fastest).

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the ref belongs to. Default: the latest snapshot.

name: PerformAction
title: Perform an accessibility action

description:
Use an app's menu bar: list its menus, or choose a command by path, e.g. ["File", "Export…"] or
["Format", "Font", "Bold"]. Matching ignores case and "…" vs "..." and accepts unambiguous
prefixes. This is often the most reliable way to run a command in a Mac app.
extras=true uses the status items at the right of the menu bar instead (Wi-Fi, Battery, an app's
icon; the system ones belong to Control Center, the default app then): a one-title path clicks the
item, opening its menu or panel (take a snapshot of that app to see a panel).
Params: path (omit to list the menus), app (default: the frontmost app), extras, depth (when
listing), report. Errors: MENU_NOT_FOUND (with the available titles), ELEMENT_NOT_ACTIONABLE
(disabled item), APP_NOT_FOUND, BLOCKED_BY_POLICY.

app.description: Target app: name ('Notes'), bundle id ('com.apple.Notes') or pid. Default: the frontmost app.

depth.description: Levels to list (1 = top-level menus only).

extras.description: Use the menu bar's status items (default app: Control Center).

path.description: Menu titles from the menu bar down, e.g. ["File", "Save As…"]. Empty = list.

report.description: What to return after acting: "diff" (what changed, default), "snapshot" (the whole new snapshot) or "none" (fastest).

name: SelectMenu
title: Use the menu bar

description: Fill several fields: labels [[label, text], …] sets each field (checkboxes take true/false), or locs [[x, y, text], …] clicks each point and replaces its text.

locs.description: [[x, y, text], …]: click each point and type.

name: MultiEdit
title: Fill a form

description:
Deal with the sheet, alert or dialog in front of an app: read it, or answer it.
action: inspect (default: its title, text, fields and buttons), accept (press the default button:
OK, Allow, Save…, else the rightmost one), cancel (press Cancel/Not Now/No, else press Escape), or
press (the button titled button). text fills the dialog's first text field before pressing.
path (open/save panels, with accept or press) first goes to that folder or file with Go to the
folder (Shift-Cmd-G), e.g. "~/Documents" or "~/Desktop/report.pdf"; for a save panel, give the
folder as path and the file name as text. Pressing a button that deletes, replaces or discards
something asks the user first. Params: app (default: the frontmost app), action, button, text,
path, report.
Errors: ELEMENT_NOT_ACTIONABLE (no dialog is open; the panel refused the path), INVALID_ARGUMENT
(no such button: the message lists them), USER_DENIED, BLOCKED_BY_POLICY (secure fields: the user
types passwords), NEEDS_USER (system authentication dialogs), USER_ACTIVE, PAUSED_BY_USER.

app.description: App name or bundle id (default: frontmost).

path.description: Open/save panels: go to this folder or file first.

report.description: What to return after acting: "diff" (what changed, default), "snapshot" (the whole new snapshot) or "none" (fastest).

text.description: Text for the dialog's first text field.

name: HandleDialog
title: Answer a dialog

description: Launch (name: app name, bundle id or .app path), switch to (bring to front) or resize apps. resize moves/resizes the app's front window to window_loc [x, y] / window_size [w, h] (screen points); launch takes them too. launch_executable opens an .app path (no args or cwd on macOS).

name.description: App name, bundle id or .app path.

window_loc.description: [x, y] for the window's top-left corner.

name: App
title: Manage an app

description:
Focus, move, resize, minimize, restore, zoom, toggle full screen or close a window.
Params: action; window_id (from list_windows) or ref (any element of a snapshot: its window);
x + y (move: the window's new top-left corner, screen points); width + height (resize).
Returns the window afterwards (frame and state); close returns closed=true (the app may ask to save
first). Errors: WINDOW_NOT_FOUND, STALE_REF, BLOCKED_BY_POLICY, INVALID_ARGUMENT.

action.description: focus | move | resize | minimize | restore | zoom | fullscreen | close.

ref.description: Any element ref of a snapshot of the window.

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the ref belongs to. Default: the latest snapshot.

name: Window
title: Manage a window

description:
Open a URL, file or folder with its default app (or with_app), or reveal a file in the Finder.
Params: target (https://…, mailto:…, x-apple.systempreferences:…, an absolute path or ~/path, or a
file:// URL), with_app (app name or bundle id), reveal (select it in a Finder window).
Only http, https, mailto, file and x-apple.systempreferences URLs are opened; other schemes are app
commands and need the scripting toolset. Without the shell tool, files that would run (.command,
executables) and anything opened with a terminal app are blocked. Returns what was opened.
Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT (empty target, missing file, relative path), BLOCKED_BY_POLICY (URL scheme,
protected app), APP_NOT_FOUND (with_app).

reveal.description: Select the file in a Finder window instead of opening it.

target.description: URL, absolute path, ~/path or file:// URL.

with_app.description: Open with this app (name or bundle id).

name: Open
title: Open a URL or file

description: Read (mode=get) or set (mode=set, text) the clipboard text.
name: Clipboard
title: Clipboard

description: Show a macOS notification with title and message.
name: Notification
title: Show a notification

description:
Find files, folders and apps with Spotlight (like typing into Spotlight, or mdfind).
Params: query (words; may be empty with a kind), kind (app, pdf, image, folder, document, text, audio, movie, presentation, spreadsheet, archive, code, email, font), scope (a folder
to search in, e.g. "~/Documents"), limit (≤ 200).
Returns absolute paths, best first; open one with the open tool.
Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT (bad kind, scope or query), TIMEOUT, NOT_SUPPORTED (Spotlight unavailable).
name: Spotlight
title: Spotlight search

description:
Facts about this Mac: macOS version and build, model, CPU, memory, uptime and load, power source
and battery, light/dark appearance and volume.
Best effort: a source that is unavailable is left out and listed under "unavailable".
name: SystemInfo
title: System information

description:
Change simple system settings: output volume (0-100), mute / unmute, light or dark appearance.
Params: action (volume | mute | unmute | appearance); level (volume); mode (appearance: light | dark).
Returns the new state. Changing the appearance may trigger a one-time Automation permission prompt
(PERMISSION_AUTOMATION until the user allows it). Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT, COMMAND_FAILED, TIMEOUT.
name: SystemControl
title: Change volume or appearance

description: List processes (mode=list, name filter, limit) or stop one (mode=kill by pid, or by name when exactly one matches; force for SIGKILL). Stopping asks the user; system processes are refused.

name.description: list: filter; kill: the process to stop.

name: Process
title: List or stop processes

description: Run a command line with zsh (PowerShell's counterpart on macOS) and return exit code, stdout and stderr; timeout in seconds. The user approves each command.

timeout.description: Seconds before it is stopped (at most [scripting] shell_timeout_s).

name: Shell
title: Run a shell command

description:
Run an AppleScript or JavaScript for Automation (JXA) script with osascript and return its result
as text. The user approves each script and sees it in full.
Use it for apps with a scripting dictionary (Mail, Calendar, Notes, Finder, Music, Safari…) when
that is more reliable than clicking, and for data the UI hides.
Params: script; language (applescript | javascript); timeout_s (default 30, at most 120).
Apps the script names are checked against the safety policy (deny_apps, and the Terminal rule:
scripting a terminal needs the shell tool), and System Events scripts against the frontmost app.
macOS asks the user once per target app for the Automation permission.
Errors: PERMISSION_AUTOMATION (not allowed to control that app), APP_NOT_FOUND, TIMEOUT,
COMMAND_FAILED (the script's own error, quoted), BLOCKED_BY_POLICY, USER_DENIED.

timeout_s.description: Seconds before the script is stopped.

name: AppleScript
title: Run AppleScript or JXA

description:
List or run the user's Apple Shortcuts (the shortcuts command, macOS 12+).
Use it to reuse automations the user already built. Params: action list | run; list: query
(case-insensitive filter), limit; run: name (exact, from list), input (text passed to the
shortcut), timeout_s (default 30, at most 600). Running asks the user first.
Returns the names, or the shortcut's output as text (cut at [scripting] output_max_chars).
Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT (no shortcut with that name), TIMEOUT (it may wait for the user),
COMMAND_FAILED, NOT_SUPPORTED (no shortcuts command), USER_DENIED.

input.description: run: text given to the shortcut.

timeout_s.description: run: seconds before it is stopped.

name: Shortcuts
title: List or run Shortcuts

description: Read or write macOS preferences (the Registry's counterpart): path is the domain (com.apple.dock, NSGlobalDomain), name the key. mode get | list | set (value, type String, DWord, Bool or Float). Writing asks the user.

path.description: Preferences domain, e.g. com.apple.dock or NSGlobalDomain.

type.description: set: String, DWord/QWord (integer), Bool or Float.

name: Defaults
title: Read or write preferences

description:
List, switch to, open or close browser tabs (Safari, Chrome, Arc, Edge, Brave, Chromium, Vivaldi).
Params: action list | activate | open | close; browser (default: the frontmost browser, else the
first running one); activate/close: window and tab numbers from list (close defaults to the
front tab); open: url (a bare host gets https://), new_window.
list returns every tab with its window and tab number, active flag, title and URL. Numbers change
when tabs open, close or windows reorder: list again before acting on old numbers.
Uses AppleScript: macOS asks the user once to let AXPilot control the browser.
Errors: APP_NOT_FOUND (browser not running), PERMISSION_AUTOMATION, INVALID_ARGUMENT (no such
window or tab, bad URL), BLOCKED_BY_POLICY (javascript:/data: URLs, protected tabs).

browser.description: Safari, Chrome, Arc, Edge, Brave, Chromium or Vivaldi (name, key or bundle id). Default: the frontmost browser, else the first one running.

new_window.description: open: in a new window instead of a new tab.

tab.description: Tab number within the window, from 1.

name: BrowserTabs
title: Browser tabs

description: Read the text of the page in the browser's front window (Safari, Chrome, Arc, Edge, Brave…). AXPilot does not fetch URLs: url, if given, must be the page shown (open it with BrowserTabs).

browser.description: Safari, Chrome, Arc, Edge, Brave… (default: frontmost).

url.description: The page you expect (it must be open in the browser).

use_dom.description: Ignored: the page is always read from the browser.

use_sampling.description: Ignored: the text is returned as is.

name: Scrape
title: Read the web page

description:
Run JavaScript in a browser tab and return its result as text (the user approves each script and
sees the page and the code). Use it to read or change page state that the accessibility tree does
not show, e.g. document.title or a form's hidden value. Prefer browser_read for reading text.
Params: js (an expression or statements; the last expression is the result), browser, window and
tab (default: the front tab).
Needs the browser's JavaScript-from-AppleScript setting: Safari: Develop → Allow JavaScript from
Apple Events; Chrome-family: View → Developer → Allow JavaScript from Apple Events.
Errors: NOT_SUPPORTED (that setting is off), PERMISSION_AUTOMATION, APP_NOT_FOUND,
INVALID_ARGUMENT (no such tab), COMMAND_FAILED (a JavaScript error), BLOCKED_BY_POLICY,
USER_DENIED.

browser.description: Safari, Chrome, Arc, Edge, Brave, Chromium or Vivaldi (name, key or bundle id). Default: the frontmost browser, else the first one running.

tab.description: Tab number within the window, from 1.

name: BrowserEvalJS
title: Run JavaScript in a tab
